persons.note: INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED RESIDENT. Originally documented in Chicago post-office evidence; independent resident research now corroborates the identity. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Clark, Erastus' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.evidence_for: Surname 'Clark' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins E. Surname 'Clark' folds to the same string as the 1844 entry's, and the given name of both begins E.
resident_research.evidence_against: The surname 'Clark' is in Fergus's death notices and no entry under it carries the initial 'E' of 'Erastus Clark'. A surname-only agreement is a refusal, here as everywhere: the list prints eleven Smiths. 'J. D. Clark' at printed page 215 line 19 (33S7-9YYJ-9WF) is NOT 'Erastus Clark': The head is written 'J. D. Clark' — a surname and initials only — and 1 person(s) of 1835 carry the surname 'clark'. A surname and a letter is not an identity. 'J. E. Clark' at printed page 226 line 5 (33S7-9YYJ-B3) is NOT 'Erastus Clark': The head is written 'J. E. Clark' — a surname and initials only — and 1 person(s) of 1835 carry the surname 'clark'. A surname and a letter is not an identity. One hundred and fifteen apparent surname hits in the volume and not one 'Erastus Clark'. The forename appears in it only as Erastus Bowen, Erastus Selden Bowen and Erastus Smith Williams, all bearing other surnames.
resident_research.summary: Independently corroborated. Erastus Clark agrees, forename for forename or initial for initial, with a record outside the post-office lists in the St Cyr / St Mary registers, the Fergus 1839/1843 and Norris 1844 directories. Surname 'Clark' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins E.
resident_research.notes: Research only. Later-volume readings are recorded here and NOT promoted: T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
